page: Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server driven by 64 physical ARMv9 cores based on the AWS Neoverse-V3 Graviton architecture operating at 3.3 GHz. The instance includes 128 GB of RAM, offering 2 GB of memory per core alongside 48 MB of L3 cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core. Managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features a 34 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs are omitted in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong multi-threaded computational capabilities and fast memory throughput. The server records top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core execution, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. PassMark benchmarks show strong memory scores, high-throughput database operations, and physics calculations, supported by Redis SET operations reaching 180.55 million operations per second and static web serving speeds of 174.71 GB/sec. Single-core stress-ng performance and CPU-driven LLM inference fall into average benchmark tiers.

The c9g.16xlarge delivers resource efficiency by offering 64 full physical cores without simultaneous multithreading overhead. The compute-oriented 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio makes this instance cost-effective for parallel CPU-bound tasks rather than memory-heavy or local storage-dependent operations. Ideal workloads include high-concurrency web serving, distributed software builds, Redis caching layers, database processing, and scientific physics simulations.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by 64 physical ARMv9 cores on the AWS Neoverse-V3 architecture operating at 3.3 GHz. Configured with 128 GB of memory, it maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a 34 Gbps baseline network interface on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, without local NVMe drives or discrete GPUs. Benchmark data showcases top-tier multi-threaded CPU performance, including exceptional scores in software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and Redis throughput exceeding 180 million operations per second. While single-core stress testing and CPU-based LLM inference deliver moderate results, its high physical core density renders it highly cost-efficient for parallelized compute tasks. The c9g.16xlarge is well suited for high-concurrency web applications, distributed software compilation, caching clusters, and parallel data processing jobs.
